root_causes.description: The frontend edge service exhibits a severe p99 tail-latency spike (max ~7004 ms, approaching the ~7 s request timeout ceiling) while p50/p95 stay ~23-25 ms, so a subset of edge requests stall until they time out/abort, generating a sustained server-side error rate. All downstream dependencies report zero server errors, localizing the fault to the frontend edge (consistent with an injected latency/timeout fault).

evidence.expected_baseline: p99 < ~50ms with no tail beyond p95 (steady-state p50/p95 ~23-25ms)
0 — confirms fault is not propagating from checkout/downstream

evidence.observed_value: frontend user_get_ads handler span = 1856ms (search_traces min_duration_ms=1000; 20 traces, p95_duration=1770079ms)
evidence.expected_baseline: frontend handler spans ~3-10ms (ok traces measured at 3-10ms)
no CPU saturation; rules out cpu_stress

root_causes.description: Alternative interpretation: requests exceeding the ~7 s ceiling are aborted at the frontend edge, producing the sustained server-side error ratio (~60% of incoming requests) with clean downstream dependencies, consistent with an injected HTTP abort rather than propagated failure.

evidence.observed_value: mean=1.289 req/s error rate sustained across full window

evidence.expected_baseline: if errors were downstream-propagated, error spans would appear here

root_causes.description: Weaker hypothesis: the frontend's ad path (user_get_ads) shows elevated latency (1856ms), so a slow 'ad' dependency could contribute to edge stalls; however no ad-service server errors were observed and the evidence is indirect.

remediation_steps: Audit the active flagd feature-flag configuration for a frontend latency/timeout injection flag and disable it to validate the root cause.
Capture and inspect frontend request traces/logs during the latency window to identify the specific handler or downstream call stalling to the ~7s timeout.

If no flag injection is found, add edge-side circuit-breaking/timeout tuning on frontend handlers (e.g. user_get_ads) and consider horizontal scaling of the frontend deployment to shed tail-latency stalls.
Monitor frontend p99 latency and server error rate after mitigation to confirm p99 returns to < ~50ms and error_rate < 0.01.
